clue.text: Escapes from rich people on cul-de-sacs

indicators.note: in an across clue, rich people on cul-de-sacs puts the rich people after the streets

parts.note: a close is a dead-end street, so cul-de-sacs are closes
the haves are the wealthy, as in 'the haves and have-nots'

explanation.surface: Getting away from the wealthy residents of quiet dead-end streets.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'close' is a short residential street, often a cul-de-sac.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow escapes from danger are idiomatically called near things or narrow squeaks; the plural phrase matches the plural noun.

clue.text: Falls for bounder in suit

indicators.note: the word for bounder sits inside the word for suit

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit
a cad is an old-fashioned word for a dishonourable man, a bounder

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles over while chasing a rogue in a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a waterfall, so plural 'Falls' as a noun suits a series of falling water, or the verb sense 'falls' in a rush.

clue.text: Award for boys regularly on wheels

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word boys, the second and fourth

parts.note: wheels is slang for a car

explanation.surface: A prize given to lads who ride around on bikes or skates.
explanation.definitionFit: The film industry's Academy Award statuette is popularly named this, so it is an example of an award.

clue.text: It proves the rule, but no one returns

parts.note: but means except, as in 'all but one'

indicators.note: the letters for no one are read backwards

parts.note: NO plus I, the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rule is proven, yet nobody comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the saying 'the exception proves the rule'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says an exception proves the rule, so the clue paraphrases a well-known saying.

clue.text: Criminal needing specs to be included in high definition

indicators.note: the specs letters go inside the abbreviation for high definition

parts.note: a pair of glasses looks like two round lenses, the letters OO

explanation.surface: A crook needs glasses to appear in a high-definition picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A hood, short for hoodlum, is a gangster or thug.

clue.text: Forceful opening across European border

indicators.note: the word for opening stretches across, around, the other two pieces

parts.note: a vent is an opening or outlet
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: A forceful opening move across a European frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement describes something showing strong feeling and intensity, so it is a synonym of forceful.

clue.text: Cornish listener's curse?

parts.note: Cornwall is in the south-west of England, abbreviated SW
an ear is what listens

explanation.surface: Asks whether a Cornish hearer's malediction is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at the south-western tip of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to utter profanity, so it is a verb synonym of curse.

clue.text: One who wields a cross in Spain with moulded Celt gold

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: the letters of the word Celt are shaped into a new order

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A Spaniard fashions a cross from Celtic gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter marks the ballot paper with an X, so a voter wields a cross; this is a witty paraphrase.

clue.text: Endearing label designed to cover the centre of Dover

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround the middle of Dover
the letters of label are arranged into a new design
the inner letters of Dover, without its first and last

explanation.surface: A label printed to stick over the middle of a sign for Dover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Designed' rearranges the letters of label, and 'to cover' wraps them around the middle of Dover.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lovable is easy to feel affection for, which is what endearing means.

clue.text: Sign of remorse seeing material on fire?

indicators.note: in an across clue, material placed on fire means it comes after

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them from a job
cloth is material

explanation.surface: Asks whether material that is burning shows penitence.
explanation.walkthrough: Sackcloth and ashes was worn in the Bible as a show of repentance.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing the coarse fabric was a traditional biblical penance, so it stands for contrition.

clue.text: Run away from revolutionary European, free at last!

indicators.note: turning round, so the word for a European is read backwards

parts.note: a Pole is a European

indicators.note: taking the final letter of the word free

explanation.surface: A rebel from Europe celebrates finally being free.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run off secretly to marry, so it is a specific sense of running away.

clue.text: Short article — very dry — about parking

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the word for very dry goes around the parking letter

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne

explanation.surface: A terse newspaper piece, extremely dull, on car parks.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrupt manner is curt, so it is a synonym of short in the sense of brusque.

clue.text: Budding setter's back with new genre, not without a negative reaction

indicators.note: the setter's word for himself is read backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me

indicators.note: the letters of genre and not are rearranged, the negative removed

parts.note: no is a negative response

explanation.surface: A new musical style, emerging from the setter, meets disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' makes EM; 'new' rearranges GENRE and NOT, and 'without' takes away NO, leaving ERGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something budding is just beginning to develop, as an emerging trend is.

clue.text: Demand points to follow

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
to tail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: An order to go after the points marked on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to require or necessitate, so as verbs it means demand.

clue.text: Revealing story supports Swiss marksman

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporter goes underneath

parts.note: William Tell is the legendary Swiss archer
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A revealing tale backs up the account of a Swiss sharpshooter.
explanation.definitionFit: A telltale sign gives something away, so the adjective means revealing.

clue.text: Barack's worried about new cafe!

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the letter for new
the letters of Barack's are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: Barack frets about a newly opened cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' rearranges BARACKS to SACKBAR, and N goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafe and a counter selling light meals are both places for quick bites, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Discoloration of skin of onions cut in pieces

indicators.note: the letters of onions cut are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Chopping onions leaves a mark on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A contusion is a bruise, which discolours the skin.

clue.text: Time to lock up for a walk in London

parts.note: bird is British slang for prison time, from rhyming slang bird-lime
to cage is to lock up

explanation.surface: A prisoner's sentence: confinement in place of a stroll around London.
explanation.walkthrough: Birdcage Walk is a street by St James's Park in London; 'doing bird' is British slang for serving a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The London street Birdcage Walk takes its name from this word, so the definition points to that place-name.

clue.text: Sheet iron reshaped as a form of entertainment

parts.note: a film is a thin sheet

indicators.note: the letters of iron are formed into a new shape

explanation.surface: Sheet metal is reformed for show purposes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark crime cinema genre is one kind of entertainment, so this is an example.

clue.text: Refusing to eat following an insect bite

parts.note: a sting is an insect's bite

explanation.surface: Someone stops eating after being bitten by a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Fasting means going without food, so it is a synonym of refusing to eat.

clue.text: Assorted nuts covering each throw

indicators.note: the mixed letters wrap around the abbreviation for each
the letters of nuts are mixed up

explanation.surface: A bowl of mixed nuts covering every throw cushion.
explanation.definitionFit: To unseat a rider is to throw them from the saddle, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Fall in support on course for novice

indicators.note: the word for fall sits inside the golf support

parts.note: a golf tee supports the ball on a golf course
rain is what falls from the sky

explanation.surface: A beginner on the golf course stumbles while propping something up.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is someone still learning, so a beginner or novice.

clue.text: Prepare a team reserve

parts.note: to set the table is to prepare it
a side is a team

explanation.surface: Getting a squad ready as substitutes.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something by for later is to keep it in reserve, so the phrasal verb matches.

clue.text: Problems for viewers in street, of course

parts.note: yes means certainly, of course

explanation.surface: Asks whether onlookers in the road naturally have trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflamed swellings on the eyelid trouble the eye, and the eye is what views.

clue.text: Country needing man with an answer

parts.note: a guy is a man

explanation.surface: A nation needs a fellow who has the solution.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a nation on the northern coast of South America.

clue.text: Politician protected by first-class defence

indicators.note: the politician sits inside the first-class letters

parts.note: A1 is first-rate, written AI
a Lib is a Liberal politician

explanation.surface: A politician shielded by a top-notch legal argument.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, used as a defence in court.

clue.text: Shred a short book

indicators.note: the word for book is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: Tearing up a brief volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Not an atom of truth means not a shred, so it is a synonym for a tiny amount.

clue.text: Type of woodwork popular with non-specialist

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
lay means not professional, as in a layman

explanation.surface: A kind of carpentry that is liked by amateurs.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorative pieces set into a wooden surface, marquetry style, are one kind of woodwork, so this is an example.

clue.text: Wearing down, turning it into art

indicators.note: the letters of it into art are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Transforming something into art by wearing it down.
explanation.definitionFit: Attrition is gradual erosion by friction, the wearing away of something.

clue.text: Rocket, say, for second eleven needing to change, lacking core

parts.note: a cricket or football team has eleven players

indicators.note: the remaining letters are rearranged
the central letter of needing is taken out

explanation.surface: A reserve side must change its lineup, lacking a heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephenson's Rocket was a famous early locomotive. 'Lacking core' removes the middle D from NEEDING, and 'to change' rearranges NEEING.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephenson's Rocket was a pioneering locomotive, so it is an example of a steam-powered locomotive.
